main_body: A flat ground tile patch (snow) filling the whole frame: a repeating grey-green base with pale blue-lilac patches, white speckle dots and dark dash marks. No standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain surface; the scan shows repeating texture runs, not a top band over a front face)
evidence: Terrain ground tile, not a standing object. The 3/4 contract does not apply to a flat repeating ground texture. There is no object body, no side face and no elevation drawing. Kind 'terrain' fits.

style.evidence: The candidate has 7 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 26 and 80 for the grass reference. It matches the paving reference, which also has 7 colours and 7 per tile. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so no large single-colour areas. The dark dashes are tinted green-grey (0% neutral), so the outline is a material tone, not a sticker line. The ramp has about 5 steps: white, pale blue, light grey-green, mid grey-green and dark green-grey. Texture comes from white speckles, blue patches and dark dashes, but the pattern repeats mechanically with a regular grid of identical motifs. It reads as a busy tiling pattern more than natural snow, and it is thinner than the grass reference. It is not shallow or sticker-like, but it is below the grass reference. Because the same kind of reference (paving) has the same colour count and the candidate is not flatter, it is acceptable but weak. Snow would normally be lighter and smoother, though hue is not judged.
